artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the triangular/hexagonal grid in the plane whose cells are unit equilateral triangles (alternately pointing up and down). Two kinds of tiles are used:

- A "stone" is the union of three pairwise-adjacent triangular cells (forming a small upward- or downward-pointing triangle); it has two orientations.
- A "bone" is the union of three triangular cells whose centers are collinear; it has three orientations (vertical, rising, falling).

Let R be a finite, simply-connected region of this grid that admits at least one tiling by stones and bones. Define two local moves ("2-flips") that replace two tiles within a tiling by two other tiles covering exactly the same cells:

(i) Replace two stones of opposite orientation by two bones.
(ii) Replace a (stone, bone) pair by a stone of the same orientation together with a bone of a different orientation.

(Each move is applied wherever such a local pair of tiles occupies a region for which the alternative pair is also a valid tiling.)

Question: Is the set of all stones-and-bones tilings of R connected under the equivalence relation generated by these 2-flip moves? In other words, can every tiling of R by stones and bones be transformed into every other such tiling by a finite sequence of 2-flips?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up extensive recent work on stones-and-bones tilings of benzels (enumerative results via compression, the abacus bijection, and the double-dimer model), but no source was found that explicitly resolves the connectivity question of the tiling space under the two specified 2-flip moves for general finite simply-connected regions. The status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Stones, Bones, and Snakes: Tilability of the hexagonal grid via the double dimer model
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on tilability of hexagonal regions by stones and bones via the double dimer model.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues on stones-and-bones tilings but does not appear to settle the 2-flip connectivity question.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of Benzels via Generalized Compression
status_evidence.snippet: Defant, Li, Propp, and Young recently resolved enumerative conjectures of Propp concerning stones-and-bones tilings of benzels.
status_evidence.claim: Recent papers address enumeration rather than the flip-connectivity of the tiling graph.
